import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Binary representation of primes that divide a number, in decimal

The value $a(n)$ is given by
$$ a(n) = \sum_{p \mid n, p \text{ prime}} 2^{\pi(p) - 1} $$
where $\pi(p) = \mathrm{primeCounting}(p)$ gives the 1-based index of the prime $p$.

*References:*
- [A087207](https://oeis.org/A087207)-/

namespace OeisA87207

/-- Binary representation of the prime factors of $n$, represented in decimal:
$a(n) = \sum_{p \in \mathrm{support}(\mathrm{factorization}(n))} 2^{\pi(p) - 1}$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ p ∈ (Nat.factorization n).support, 2 ^ (Nat.primeCounting p - 1)

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 0 := by decide +native

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by decide +native

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 1 := by decide +native

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 2 := by decide +native

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 1 := by decide +native

/--
Starting at any $n$ and iterating the map $n \mapsto a(n)$, we will always reach $0$.
- _Antti Karttunen_, Jun 18,20 2017
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) : ∃ k : ℕ, (a^[k]) n = 0 := by
  sorry

end OeisA87207

reformulations.difference: OEIS indexes A087207 from 1; Lean extends the map by a 0 = 0, quantifies over all natural starting values, and allows zero iterations.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive inputs, factorization support is exactly the set of distinct prime divisors, and primeCounting p - 1 gives the required bit position. The additional starting value 0 satisfies the conclusion with k = 0. For positive starting values, zero iterations cannot reach 0. Moreover, because a 0 = 0, any successful iteration count can be increased by one. Thus the Lean statement is equivalent to requiring every positive starting value to reach zero after a positive number of iterations. Review.conjecture_equiv_positive_form in /workspace/review/scratch.lean proves this equivalence without using the conjecture or sorry.

review.notes: Checked all seven declarations. The conjecture matches Karttunen's June 2017 OEIS comment verbatim. Lean verified all 69 listed sequence values, the examples a(38) = 129 and a(140) = 13, boundary cases, and sample orbits. General proofs confirm the distinct-prime support and prime-index exponent. OEIS's main entry pages were blocked by Cloudflare, so their text was read through the official OEIS export dated 2026-09-07; the b-file was accessible directly. A087207 and A288569 still record the claim as conjectural. The reviewed file was not modified.
